steps: Open the live page (https://jpavia10.github.io/prometheus-hub/pillars/aether/) on a phone-sized browser and use every section.
Read the code (https://github.com/jpavia10/prometheus-hub/tree/main/pillars/aether): every file the page loads, and pillar.json.
Write section A from what is there now, with file:line for each item; then B to H.
Write for Claude to build from: exact, testable, nothing vague like 'improve the UX'.

deliver.shape: one markdown file with exactly these headings, in this order: A What it does today | B What Joseph needs it to do | C Data | D Screens | E Rules and edge cases | F Acceptance tests | G Order of work | H Must not

fields.name: A What it does today
fields.rule: every section, control and number on the live page, each with the file and line in the code that makes it (e.g. app.js:142)

fields.name: B What Joseph needs it to do
fields.rule: 'As Joseph, when ..., I want ..., so that ...'; from the pillar's mission and its own data; never invent facts about his life

fields.name: C Data
fields.rule: record | field | type | unit | required | example | storage key (prometheus.<pillar>.<name>) | read by which other pillar

fields.name: D Screens
fields.rule: purpose; every element top to bottom; every number with its formula and source field; the empty state text; the error state

fields.name: E Rules and edge cases
fields.rule: dates and time zones, missing data, offline, two devices, a value of 0 vs unknown

fields.name: F Acceptance tests
fields.rule: Given / When / Then, each checkable in a phone browser in under two minutes

fields.name: G Order of work
fields.rule: each step small enough for one build, with what Joseph can use after it

fields.name: H Must not
fields.rule: the charter's protections that apply, no server or account, no made-up numbers

tasks.why: Aether gets sun times from the USNO API, so offline (or when the API is down) it has none. A mountain field lab needs dawn and dusk without signal.
tasks.unlocks: Aether shows today's light schedule offline for any date and place, checked against USNO.
inputs: NOAA 'General Solar Position Calculations' (gml.noaa.gov) and the NOAA Solar Calculator page
steps: Write one plain JavaScript file (no imports, no libraries, under 160 lines) that defines window.AETHER_SUN = { times(dateISO, lat, lon, tzOffsetHours) }. It returns { astroDawn, nauticalDawn, civilDawn, sunrise, noon, sunset, civilDusk, nauticalDusk, astroDusk } as local 'HH:MM' strings, null when the event does not happen that day. Use the NOAA equations (cite the document in a comment): solar declination, equation of time, hour angle for zenith 90.833, 96, 102 and 108 degrees.

Make 12 test vectors for Frazier Park (34.8228, -118.9445) from the USNO API itself: https://aa.usno.navy.mil/api/rstt/oneday?date=YYYY-MM-DD&coords=34.8228,-118.9445&tz=-8 (tz -7 on daylight-time dates). Dates: 2026-12-21, 2027-01-15, 2027-02-15, 2027-03-14, 2027-03-20, 2027-04-15, 2027-06-21, 2027-08-15, 2027-09-23, 2027-10-15, 2027-11-07, 2027-12-21. Copy USNO's begin civil twilight, rise, upper transit, set and end civil twilight exactly as its JSON gives them, with the exact API URL per vector.
Your times() must match every USNO value within 2 minutes. Run it yourself on the 12 vectors and include the result table (expected, got, difference in minutes) in the test file's 'run' field.

deliver.shape: the .js file and a JSON object {vectors: [12 x {date, tz, url, usno: {civilDawn, sunrise, noon, sunset, civilDusk}}], run: [12 x {date, field, expected, got, diff_min}]}

self_check: The .js file runs in a browser with nothing else loaded and defines window.AETHER_SUN.
Every USNO value is copied from the API response at the URL given.
Every difference in 'run' is 2 minutes or less.
tasks.done_when: Claude runs times() on all 12 vectors and every value is within 2 minutes of USNO.
checks: Claude runs the file in Node with the 12 vectors.
Claude opens 3 of the USNO URLs and compares.
rejected_if: any value more than 2 minutes from USNO
a library, import or network call in the .js file
a USNO value that is not what its URL returns
files saved anywhere but the folder named here
